svg.title: Ionic & covalent bonds
svg.desc: Electron transfer: Metal atoms lose electrons → positive ions. Non-metals gain → negative ions. Protons stay unchanged. Group 1/2: +1/+2 ions; Group 7/6: −1/−2 ions. Electron arrangements match a noble gas. Charge → formula: Balance total charges: Mg²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → MgCl₂; 2Na⁺ + O²⁻ → Na₂O. Dot-and-cross ionic diagrams: brackets, ion charge and full outer shells; distinguish electron origins. Ionic lattice: A giant, repeating 3D arrangement of opposite ions, with strong electrostatic attractions in all directions. Many attractions need much energy to overcome → high melting/boiling. Not separate molecules. Conductivity follows movement: Solid: ions held in fixed positions → cannot carry charge through it. Molten/dissolved: ions free to move → conducts. Electrons do not carry current through the ionic liquid. Covalent pairs: A single bond shares one pair; double shares two; triple shares three. H₂, Cl₂, HCl: one single bond. O₂: double. N₂: triple. H₂O: two single; NH₃: three; CH₄: four. Show lone pairs too: O has two in H₂O; N has one in NH₃; Cl has three. Molecules & models: Strong bonds inside a molecule; weaker intermolecular forces between molecules. Boiling overcomes those forces. Bigger molecules generally have stronger intermolecular forces. No mobile ions/electrons → no conduction. 2D formulae omit 3D shape; ball-and-stick bonds are not literal rods.
